Plot the Gini index of each sample

Source: R/quality_control.R
plot_gini.Rd

Plots the Gini index of each sample computed with compute_gini: 0 means that all the barcodes have the same number of reads, values close to 1 that a few barcodes take most of the reads. In a dropout screen it usually increases over time; a strong increase or a large difference between replicates can signal a bottleneck.

Usage

plot_gini(screenR_Object, palette = NULL, alpha = 1, legende_position = "none")

Arguments

screenR_Object

The ScreenR object obtained using create_screenr_object.

palette

An optional vector of colors, one for each sample.

alpha

The opacity of the bars, between 0 and 1. Default 1.

legende_position

The position of the legend: "none" (default), "top", "bottom", "right" or "left".

Value

A ggplot object.

See also

compute_gini, plot_barcode_lost

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))
plot_gini(object)
